corrections.why: The register gives a 60-foot Aermotor LS-40 tower and Wikipedia gives 60 feet (18 m); the record's 20.0 m does not match either source.

corrections.proposed: SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry
corrections.why: The college says it now stewards the property and it restored the tower; the register's DEC attribution is the historic administrator.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says staffed until 1970; Wikipedia says the tower closed at the end of the 1979 season. Both are kept as events and the story reports the disagreement.
The register credits the NY Dept. of Conservation; Wikipedia credits the Civilian Conservation Corps. The story reports both.
The register lists 2,690 ft (820 m); Wikipedia lists 2,664 ft (812 m). The record keeps the register's 819.9 m.
The register describes a 3-mile trail; the college describes a four-mile trail.
The register says administered by the NY Dept. of Environmental Conservation; the college says it stewards the property today. The facts use the college as current steward.

notes_for_editor: andyarthur.org returned HTTP 403 in the cache and was not used. The NYSDEC fire-towers page was not read. The Oct. 14, 2025 ribbon cutting is only reported as scheduled; no post-event source was read, so the reopening is not confirmed. Climbing permission is not stated outright, so the visit fields stay with trail details only. Brief's record height of 20.0 m appears to be an error (60 ft = 18.3 m). The 1932 Huntington donation to SUNY appeared only in a search snippet and is not used.
